summary.sentence: 99 new papers found since 2026-05-01, plus 2 from our back catalogue. 6 carried numbers a law of ours takes: 40 separate checks (31 by the Lean kernel, 9 by a rank-direction script), 28 inside the law and 12 outside. 2 papers were inside on every check. 95 papers could not be checked, for 6 reasons:

reasons.plain: the search matched but the paper is about something else
only the abstract is open, and it does not carry the numbers
some of the numbers a law needs are there, at least one is missing
relevant, but it reports nothing our laws take as input
it makes a quantitative claim that no law of ours covers yet
it is about the organisms we keep sealed for the final test

laws.says: Cruising swimmers beat their tails so that frequency x amplitude / speed falls between 0.2 and 0.4.
laws.kind: empirical band, not a proved law; the Lean file proves only how the band follows from the frequency-speed line

laws.says: A swimmer this small and slow is in the viscous regime: density x speed x size / viscosity is below 1.
laws.kind: regime check in water (kinematic viscosity 1e-6 m2/s), integer arithmetic

laws.kind: model identity, tested here within a factor of 1.5; the tolerance is our convention

short.title: A Physical Adaptive Material Motor Unit Neural Network: A Hygromorph Composite Material Machine.
missing: h_mm (only per-layer print heights are given, no total)
deps (only shrinkage values cited from another paper)
short.why: A 4D-printed wood/PLA hygromorph actuator array driven mainly by voltage; it reports light output and an actuation strain of the aperture width, not curvature, total thickness or its own swelling strain.

short.title: Photothermally Responsive Poly(vinyl alcohol)/Polyaniline Nanoparticle Composite Hydrogels Prepared by a Facile Aqueous Route.
short.usecase_title: Crosslinker dose against stiffness and swelling
missing: series (citric acid is fixed at 20% w/w; the quantity varied is polyaniline nanoparticle loading, a filler)
short.why: Citric acid-crosslinked PVA films where the crosslinker dose never changes, so there is no crosslinker dose series to test.

short.title: Celecoxib-Loaded "Nano-in-Nano" Hierarchical Delivery System: Structure-Driven Synergistic Optimization of Diffusion Efficiency and Mechanical Stability for Osteoarthritis Therapy.
short.usecase_title: Crosslinker dose against stiffness and swelling
missing: series (a single genipin condition, 1% w/v for 30 minutes; one modulus and one swelling value)
short.why: A drug-delivery membrane with a genipin-crosslinked gelatin layer made at one genipin dose, so there is no dose series.

short.title: Effects of Test-Section Length and Cross-Sectional Blockage on the Swimming Performance of Juvenile Grass Carp: Implications for Standardized Testing and Fish-Passage Design.
short.usecase_title: Swimming: tail-beat frequency, amplitude and speed
missing: u_m_s (the text gives tail-beat frequency and amplitude only as start-to-end ranges; the flow speed for each value is only in Figures 3 and 6)
short.why: Juvenile grass carp in a swim tunnel with tail-beat frequency (Hz) and peak-to-peak amplitude (in body lengths) stated, but never paired in the text with the speed at which they were measured.

short.title: Single-cell transcriptional dynamics in a living vertebrate.
short.usecase_title: Zebrafish body plan: somites and segmentation clock
missing: t_min (stated only as cited background, not measured here)
short.why: Live imaging of her1 transcription in the zebrafish segmentation clock; a clock period (~30 min at 28 C) is stated only as background citing earlier work, and no somite length or wavefront speed is given (Europe PMC fullTextXML gave HTTP 500, text read from the public NCBI efetch copy of the same PMCID).

short.title: Gelatin Hydrogel Crosslinking: From Molecular Design to Functional Soft Materials.
short.usecase_title: Crosslinker dose against stiffness and swelling
missing: a dose series measured in this paper
short.why: The only dose series is quoted second-hand: this review tabulates it from another paper, which the reader did not open. Numbers must come from the paper that measured them, so it was not checked.

short.title: Development of a compartmentalized silk fibroin-reinforced GelMA hydrogel platform for kidney-inspired tissue engineering.
short.usecase_title: Crosslinker dose against stiffness and swelling
missing: doses (only two crosslinker levels are used: 200 and 400 µL HEMA; three are needed)
short.why: The gels are made at only two crosslinker amounts (low and high), each at two silk contents, so there is no three-point crosslinker series; stiffness is printed for the four recipes (0.73, 0.93, 2.14, 2.94 kPa) and is higher at the higher crosslinker amount.

short.title: Cycles upon cycles-Temperature scaling of medaka development.
short.usecase_title: Zebrafish body plan: somites and segmentation clock
short.why: The paper measures the medaka segmentation clock and tail elongation at 22, 27 and 32 °C, but the main text prints only the clock period (80 min at 27 °C); somite size and elongation speed appear only in figures and the supplement.

short.title: A transient nonlinear finite element framework and implementation of coupled electro-chemo-mechanics of polyelectrolyte hydrogels
short.why: A computer simulation of a swelling gel on a rubber layer prints the sheet thickness ("a height of h=0.5 mm", Section 5.2) but shows the bending curvature only as plotted curves (Figure 10), and it is simulated rather than measured; no swelling-strain difference between the layers is printed.

short.title: Strouhal-Aware Model Predictive Control for Efficient Multi-Fin Flapping Locomotion
short.usecase_title: Swimming: tail-beat frequency, amplitude and speed
short.why: A four-fin underwater robot is tested at printed cruising speeds of 0.1 to 0.4 m/s (Table V) and the paper prints Strouhal-number errors, but it never prints the fin-beat frequency or the peak-to-peak amplitude for those trials (only that the fin frequency is "around 3Hz in the maximum case").

short.title: A light-response bilayer actuator for light-controlled capsule system.
short.why: A two-layer film that curls when light heats it has its total thickness printed ("a total film thickness of approximately 175 μm"), but its bending is given as angles in the text and curvature only in plots, and the layers differ in thermal expansion (printed coefficients 200e-6/K and 80e-6/K), not in swelling strain.

short.title: Physical and Mechanical Characterisation of 3D-Bioprinted Hydrogels for Dental Applications: A Scoping Review.
short.usecase_title: Crosslinker dose against stiffness and swelling
missing: a third dose and value (only two genipin concentrations are printed)
short.why: This review quotes another study's swelling at just two genipin crosslinker levels ("0.5% genipin showing the highest swelling at 8.2, and 2.5% genipin the lowest at 6.8"); the law needs at least three doses, and the numbers are second-hand from the cited study (ref. 81), which was not opened.

short.title: Decoupled Online-Inertia-Tunable Robotic Fish: Design, Modeling and Performance Analysis.
short.usecase_title: Swimming: tail-beat frequency, amplitude and speed
short.why: A robotic fish paper that prints tail-beat frequencies (1 to 5 Hz) and Strouhal numbers (for example "from 0.54 to 0.51 at 2 Hz"), but the tail amplitude and swimming speed behind them appear only in plots, not as printed values.

short.title: Chlamylipo, a Chlamydomonas-in-liposome microswimmer: Self-propelled swimming and associated lipid membrane flow.
short.why: The speed is printed (8.0 micrometres per second), but the body size appears only as a fitting parameter of a flow model, not as a measurement of the swimmers, so the check was not run.

short.title: Heterochrony of axis segmentation underlies extreme morphogenesis in the Japanese eel
short.usecase_title: Zebrafish body plan: somites and segmentation clock
missing: s_um at the same stage as the printed period
short.why: The eel-embryo preprint prints a segment-making period ("an overall periodicity of somite formation of ~25 minutes" at the 16-47 somite stages) and a minimum segment length ("~7 µm", reached from about the 47-somite stage on), but no wavefront or axis-growth speed, and the two printed numbers are not from the same stage; other segment lengths are only in plots.

short.title: All-in-one optically interactive soft robots with embedded liquid crystal holography.
short.why: A humidity- and light-driven two-layer film (liquid crystal network on silk fibroin); the layer thicknesses are printed (50 micrometre and 30 micrometre layers) but the curvature is shown only in plots and no swelling strain is given.

short.title: Enhanced Physico-Mechanical Properties of Sericin-PVA Composite Films with a Potential Antibacterial and Controlled Drug Release Features for Wound Dressing.
short.usecase_title: Crosslinker dose against stiffness and swelling
missing: doses (only one glutaraldehyde level, 3%, was used; the three films differ by silk species, not crosslinker amount)
short.why: Sericin-PVA wound films crosslinked with glutaraldehyde; stiffness is printed for three films (25.0, 78.8 and 47.8 MPa) but all were made at one crosslinker level, so there is no dose series.

short.title: Thyroid hormone determines energy efficiency of locomotion in zebrafish (Danio rerio) in a temperature-sensitive manner.
short.usecase_title: Swimming: tail-beat frequency, amplitude and speed
short.why: Zebrafish were filmed swimming at two printed speeds (0.16 and 0.28 m/s) to measure tail-beat frequency and amplitude, but those two measurements appear only in figures, not as printed numbers.

short.title: From Biological Mechanisms to Task-Oriented Design Principles: A Critical Review of Fish-like Biomimetic Robots.
short.usecase_title: Swimming: tail-beat frequency, amplitude and speed
short.why: A review of fish-like robots; its Table 4 prints top speeds for several robots (for example 0.70 m/s and 0.47 m/s) but not the tail-beat frequency and tail amplitude that go with them.
